niche.habitat: Subglacial ocean near cryovolcanic vents on the inner moon
niche.diet: Chemosynthetic biomass, dissolved H2/H2S, organic detritus

body: Translucent gelatinous medusa-analogue with six ruffled filter-fronds, ventral chemoreceptor pores, and a dorsal bioluminescent lure

links: High flux of particulate organics from vent plumes
Tidal heating drives cryovolcanic eruptions and plumes

skill.effect: Cycles fronds to clear clogs and restore efficiency by 40%

chains.weakness: Fronds tangle in dense debris flows from icequakes
observe: Six fronds pulsing rhythmically to draw water inward
Ruffled edges catching dark particulate snow
Steady expansion and contraction of the bell

journal.en: It wears the vent's breath like a gossamer coat, sifting fire and life in the dark.

plausibility.summary: Cryovolcanic and hydrothermal plumes on a tidally heated ice moon (F18) carry particulate organic matter and microbial flocs, analogous to marine snow and vent-associated particles on Earth; a gelatinous zooplankton-grade filter feeder that increases capture area is mechanically sound at moon-ocean pressures if structures are mucus-supported webs rather than rigid grids. At 1.36 g on the planet this body plan would not work on land; in a subsurface ocean buoyancy support makes large soft filters feasible.
fixes: Cryovolcanic and hydrothermal plumes on a tidally heated ice moon (F18) carry particulate organic matter and microbial flocs, analogous to marine snow and vent-associated particles on Earth; a gelatinous zooplankton-grade filter feeder that increases capture area is mechanically sound at moon-ocean pressures if structures are mucus-supported webs rather than rigid grids. At 1.36 g on the planet this body plan would not work on land; in a subsurface ocean buoyancy support makes large soft filters feasible.

analogues.organism: Larvacean Oikopleura mucous house and giant larvacean filters; salp pylosome chains; sponges and cold-seep barnacles on particulate and bacterial flux.

journal.en: A living compass nose, it tastes the world's hidden heartbeat.

plausibility.summary: H2S, H2, CH4 and redox boundaries at vents (F18, F19) produce steep chemical microgradients; vent animals orient to plumes using chemoreception, often combined with flow sensing. Electric microgradients can exist across redox interfaces but are weaker than chemistry for macroscopic navigation; pores quivering toward enriched water is consistent with selection for plume-tracking.

links: Gelatinous body relies on buoyancy over skeletal support
Low structural load allows soft tissue in water
Small moon mass yields low surface gravity and weak tidal stress on body

observe: Translucent gelatinous bell distending with gas vesicles
Slow, drifting movement with minimal limb effort

journal.en: A bubble of flesh, it forgets it is solid, suspended in the moon's cold blood.

plausibility.summary: Root trait in moon low g + hydrostatic support, not F16. Replace gas veins with lipid-rich mesoglea or ammonium-ion jelly for near-neutral buoyancy; add weakness to rapid pressure swings from cryovolcanic paroxysms. Treat gel-stored thermal energy from plumes (secret) as highly speculative—prefer high vent tolerance and slow metabolism unless you model explicit heat-storage polymers like some desert seeds, which has no strong vent-animal analogue.

moments: It hangs in the dark like a ghost of the vent, drinking the fire to sustain a body of water and dreams, its light pulsing a slow rhythm against the crushing silence.

journal.en: It hangs in the dark like a ghost of the vent, drinking the fire to sustain a body of water and dreams.
Six fronds, six tastes, one slow life filtering the world's blood.
